explanation: The derivatives of −sin(x) cycle through −sin(x), −cos(x), sin(x), and cos(x), so A is finite. Near x = 0, −csc(x) behaves like −1/x and cot(x) like 1/x. Their nth derivatives have nonzero leading terms proportional to x^(−n−1), so different derivative orders give distinct functions. Thus B and C are infinite.
